The differential equation that generates the slope field shown above is given by ${y}^{′}=(x-a)(x-b).$ Find the value of $a+b.$
worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14044310/assets/012fe788fa1ac778b361fe62c3f70344546c6c5008fa6dcce536cc721d4ba5e9.png)

 

Notice that the slopes of the slope field are horizontal along the lines $x=-2$ and $x=1,$ as shown above. Therefore, the right-hand side of the differential equation should evaluate to zero on both of these lines.

So, our differential equation must be

$$
{y}^{′}=(x+2)(x-1).
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $a=-2,b=1$ and $a+b=-1.$
